caption: Shaadi season mein ek shaam, teen shaadi! Shagun do, dulhan ke saath selfie lo, dinner karo aur agli ko tag karo. Is December aapko kitni shaadiyan attend karni hain?

web.title: Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam: Shaadi Relay Kitty Party Game Rules
web.description: Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam is a funny shaadi season relay game for kitty parties: shagun, selfie, dinner and a baraat dance twist. Rules, materials, steps and tips.
web.intro: Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam is a shaadi season relay game for kitty parties where each lady "attends" three weddings in one evening: she puts shagun in an envelope at Hall 1, takes a selfie with a cushion dulhan at Hall 2, and eats one piece of namkeen dinner at Hall 3 before tagging the next lady. The first team whose last lady gets back to the start line wins. The crazy twist: whenever the host shouts "Baraat aa gayi!" the runner must stop wherever she is and do 5 seconds of baraat dance. It fits December, when everyone has three shaadis on the same date, and it needs only chairs, envelopes, toffees, a cushion, a dupatta and namkeen.
materials: 3 chairs or stools per team (6 for two teams)
One envelope and one toffee per lady
A bowl on each Hall 1 chair to collect the shagun
A cushion with a red dupatta draped over it as the dulhan, one per team
A katori of namkeen per team, one piece per lady
A phone or speaker with a baraat song for the twist
steps: Split the ladies into two teams. For each team, set three chairs in a line a few steps apart and label them Hall 1 Shagun, Hall 2 Photo and Hall 3 Dinner. The team lines up behind a start line.
At Hall 1 the first lady picks up an envelope, puts one toffee inside as shagun, closes the flap and drops it in the bowl on the chair.
At Hall 2 she takes a selfie on her own phone with the cushion dulhan, holding the pose for 3 seconds while a teammate counts out loud.
At Hall 3 she eats one piece of namkeen as her shaadi dinner, then walks fast back to the start line and tags the next lady, who sets off to Hall 1.
Any time during the relay, the host plays a baraat song and shouts "Baraat aa gayi!". Every runner must stop where she is and dance for 5 seconds before moving on.
rules: An envelope left open does not count: the lady goes back to Hall 1 and closes it.
A runner who does not dance on "Baraat aa gayi!" must stand still and count to 10.
No running and no pushing. A lady who runs or pushes goes back to the start line.
The team whose last lady reaches the start line first wins the round.
variations: Let the host pick the Hall 2 pose: varmala, bidaai hug or jhumka check.
Mummy ji rule: at every hall the lady must say "Kitni pyaari dulhan!" loudly before her task counts.
Saree rule: every lady walks the halls with her pallu over her head like a guest at a traditional wedding.
For 3 teams, add three more chairs or run the teams one after the other with a phone timer.
tips: Keep the chairs away from walls, glass tables and the kitchen door.
Use toffees and namkeen that the ladies will happily eat, so nothing is wasted.
Call "Baraat aa gayi!" two or three times per relay, when the race is closest.
Keep the shagun envelopes and give them to the winning team as their prize.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam?
faq.a: It works best with 8 to 20 ladies split into two teams. Every lady runs the three halls once, so a full relay takes 10 to 15 minutes.

faq.q: What do you need to play Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam?
faq.a: Three chairs per team, an envelope and a toffee for each lady, a bowl, a cushion with a red dupatta as the dulhan, a katori of namkeen and a phone for the baraat song.

faq.q: Is Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam good for a shaadi theme kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. It turns the December rush of attending three weddings in one evening into a relay, so it suits shaadi season, sangeet and bridal theme kitties.

faq.q: Is this relay game safe for older ladies?
faq.a: Yes. The rule is to walk fast, never run, and chairs are kept away from walls and glass. The baraat dance can be as gentle as a few claps and a shoulder shake.

faq.q: How do you win Teen Shaadi Ek Shaam?
faq.a: The team whose last lady finishes all three halls and gets back to the start line first wins. Open envelopes and skipped dances cost time, so neat and quick wins.
